title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing rollout plan for Redwood Dedicated pilot -> production cutover. Discussed canary strategy, A/B options, monitoring and alerting, rollback criteria, runbooks and key dates. Action items assigned for runbook, benchmarks, and legal/data retention. Agreement to target mid-March canary and late-March broader cutover pending capacity and monitoring setup.
topics: Runbooks, rollback criteria, and ops handoff
Capacity / sizing for Redwood Dedicated nodes
action_items: Sarah Patel: Share rollout runbook draft (due 2026-03-06)
Marcus Li: Provide benchmark summary and quantization sizing recommendations + dedicated capacity sheet (due 2026-03-06)
Liam O'Connor: Confirm maintenance window for cutover and any blackout dates (due 2026-03-08)
Priya Desai: Finalize stakeholder list for go/no-go by 2026-03-10
Legal (BrightCare): Confirm data retention / audit log requirements (due 2026-03-10)
next_steps: Redwood to send runbook + canary playbook
Customer to provision staging VPC peering and share target subnet info
Set up synthetic traffic tests and Grafana dashboards (Redwood + BrightCare monitors)
Plan full cutover late March pending canary results
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — can you see me and audio okay?
[00:06] Aisha (CTO): Yes, looks good.
[00:09] Marcus (SE): Great, we'll keep this to about 55 minutes, agenda sent earlier — rollout plan, canary, monitoring, runbooks, open questions.
[00:18] Liam (Lead SRE): Sounds good. We had the infra sync yesterday, so this is mostly go-live planning.
[00:24] Sarah: Right. Quick status — you've been running the pilot on Dedicated for two weeks, any surprises? Marcus, do you want to call out numbers?
[00:33] Marcus: Sure. So nominal p95 latency for the endpoint on your sample traffic is around 220ms when batch size is 8; CPU/GPU utilization steady at 62-70%. There was one spike during a long context run — KV cache warmup took longer than expected, a bit of DNS flake, but nothing catastrophic.
[00:50] Priya (PM): We saw a few user-facing slow responses during our internal load test, about 1 in 2,000 requests. We logged it.
[00:56] Marcus: Right, that's the KV cache cold-start behavior. We recommended prefix caching and slight change to batching — that cut incidence by ~80% in the last run.
[01:08] Aisha: For go-live we need clear rollback criteria and who owns the ops window. Also data retention — because of PHI we need retention guarantees and audit logs.
[01:18] Sarah: Absolutely. That's on the runbook. We'll include an explicit rollback checklist and audit log locations. Marcus, can you outline the canary strategy options?
[01:27] Marcus: We reviewed two options: a canary with 5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated and 95% staying on the current internal model, or an A/B variant where we route 50/50 for specific customer cohorts. For minimal risk I'd prefer the 5% canary for the initial cutover.
[01:40] Liam: 5% is fine but we need synthetic traffic running that mirrors production headers. Also need clear SLOs — set alerts at p95>400ms or error rate >0.5% to abort.
[01:50] Priya: What about model fallbacks? If Dedicated hits capacity we should fallback to the hosted API or a smaller model automatically.
[01:57] Marcus: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We'll include the fallback policy in the runbook. Note — there may be small behavior diffs between model variants, we'll document expected delta.
[02:09] Aisha: On security: we need KMS integration, audit logs retention for 7 years, and SOC 2 evidence. Legal will boil this down but want initial confirmation.
[02:19] Sarah: We can provide SOC 2 docs and KMS integration notes. For retention we'll align with your legal; Redwood can configure audit retention per account — need the exact retention period.
[02:29] Liam: We'll confirm the retention date. Also, if we do a rolling cutover across regions, network egress costs are a concern. Show us the post-cutover cost delta in the dedicated sizing sheet.
[02:39] Marcus: Got it. I will include cost delta estimates based on your observed token distributions.
[02:44] Sarah: Let's talk timeline — target dates? We suggested canary week starting 2026-03-18 with a 3-day canary and evaluation window. Full cutover around 2026-03-25 if canary passes. Thoughts?
[02:56] Priya: That timeline works but we need at least one week for ops to validate dashboarding.
[03:01] Liam: Confirm blackout windows — we cannot do cutover during our scheduled maintenance on 2026-03-20.
[03:06] Sarah: Noted — we'll avoid that. So proposed canary 3/18-3/20 but we'll shift if needed.
[03:12] Marcus: On monitoring — recommended stack: synthetic traffic feeding two dashboards: one in Redwood Console for token-level latency and costs, and one in BrightCare Grafana for business metrics. Alerts wired into PagerDuty and a Slack channel.
[03:26] Aisha: Can you list exact alert thresholds? We need that to sign off with ops.
[03:30] Marcus: Sure — propose p95 latency >400ms, error rate >0.5%, model mismatch score >0.08 (we'll send delta metric), cost per 1k tokens spike >20% over baseline. We'll provide a monitoring spec doc.
[03:44] Priya: Model mismatch score — can you quickly explain that?
[03:47] Marcus: It's our eval metric comparing selected prompt/response distribution to baseline; basically if responses deviate significantly from expected distribution we flag. It's noisy at low volumes so only considered after a minimum sample size.
[03:58] Sarah: Back to runbooks — we should have: pre-cutover checklist, canary playbook, escalation path, rollback procedure, post-cutover validation, and communication templates. Marcus will draft technical runbook; Sarah will add stakeholder comms.
[04:12] Marcus: I'll include the exact kubectl / infra steps for Dedicated nodes, the autoscaling knobs, and KV cache priming steps. There may be some infra names transcribed weird — e.g., VPC peering should be your staging-peering-01.
[04:26] Liam: We'll share the exact subnet and peering names after the call. Priya will share the stakeholder email list.
[04:33] Aisha: One risk — data residency for EU patients. If traffic crosses regions we need to ensure data doesn't land in other regions. Is Redwood Private required?
[04:43] Sarah: For residency we can deploy Redwood Private in your VPC or use region-bound Dedicated capacity. For this pilot we recommended region-bound Dedicated — less friction than full Private. We'll include both paths in the runbook.
[04:56] Priya: For canary validation what are the success criteria? Need clear go/no-go gates.
[04:59] Marcus: Proposed gates: 1) No SLO breaches during canary, 2) Error rate <=0.2% for canary cohort, 3) No critical security findings, 4) Data retention config validated. If any gate fails, abort and rollback.
[05:14] Liam: Also require manual sign-off from ops and product. Priya and Liam to be signers.
[05:19] Sarah: Okay. Let's discuss A/B alternative briefly — that helps measure behavioral quality. But it doubles complexity for monitoring and deduping. For initial run we recommend canary only, then do an A/B test after stable cutover.
[05:32] Priya: Agreed. We'll do canary first.
[05:35] Marcus: A few operational notes: autoscaling buffer should be set to 30% during canary, and burst capacity enabled in case of traffic spikes. We'll set a hard cap to avoid runaway costs.
[05:46] Aisha: Costs — please send a delta and estimate for the canary period and monthly if we go full Dedicated.
[05:51] Marcus: Will do. I'll include token mix sensitivity and quantization profile; note that q4 int8 gave a ~2x cost drop in our lab, but there is slight model quality tradeoff.
[06:03] Priya: Is it possible to have a fallback to a quantized variant automatically in overload?
[06:08] Marcus: Yes, routing policies can fallback to a quantized model variant. We'll document expected quality delta and when to enable it (post-cutover ops decision).
[06:18] Sarah: Anything on the legal side? Priya, you said legal would confirm retention.
[06:22] Priya: Yes. We'll get that this week — 7 years is what Aisha mentioned but need written confirmation.
[06:27] Aisha: Also need to see SOC 2 and encryption docs.
[06:31] Sarah: We'll attach SOC 2 package and KMS integration notes to the runbook share.
[06:36] Marcus: Re: runbook distribution — I'll share a Google Doc and a flattened PDF for ops. Also include a one-page comms template for notifying customers of partial rollout.
[06:44] Liam: On telemetry — make sure all request/response IDs are passed through so we can correlate traces between Redwood and our services.
[06:50] Marcus: We'll add request_id passthrough guidance.
[06:53] Sarah: Ok next — who takes what. I'll list action items. Marcus — benchmarks + capacity + cost sheet. Sarah — runbook draft + comms template. BrightCare: confirm retention + maintenance window + stakeholder list. Legal: confirm retention and sign off.
[07:07] Priya: Sounds good.
[07:09] Aisha: Quick question — if canary shows subtle degradation in quality, what threshold do we use to decide to proceed?
[07:16] Marcus: We'll use the model mismatch score threshold I mentioned plus manual review of a sampled prompt set. If mismatch >0.08 but business metrics unchanged we can consider a partial rollback or extended canary. We'll define an escalation ladder.
[07:31] Sarah: Anything else on runbook contents?
[07:34] Liam: Add a step to validate encryption-at-rest keys and that KMS rotates keys per policy.
[07:39] Sarah: We'll include that.
[07:42] Marcus: Also adding a short checklist for KV cache priming: seed with top 100 prefixes, run warmup script with synthetic requests, verify hit rate >90% before routing live traffic.
[07:55] Priya: Can you share that warmup script?
[07:58] Marcus: Yes, will attach to the runbook.
[08:01] Sarah: Okay let's talk about communication cadence during canary — daily stand at 10:30, and a go/no-go review 24 hours after the first full day.
[08:11] Priya: 10:30 works for ops.
[08:14] Aisha: We'll need a public facing status page entry template for customer comms in case of visible incidents.
[08:20] Sarah: We'll include the template.
[08:23] Marcus: Any concerns about infra naming or permissions? We need IAM role with limited privileges for Dedicated nodes and service accounts.
[08:30] Liam: We'll provision roles; I'll share the role ARN.
[08:34] Sarah: Timing check — we're at 30 mins. Anything else?
[08:38] Priya: Quick note — we might need an exec-level slide for go-live decision on March 24. Can Redwood help prepare a one-pager?
[08:45] Sarah: Yes, we'll prepare an exec one-pager summarizing canary metrics, risks, and recommended decision.
[08:50] Marcus: I'll include a short benchmark appendix.
[08:53] Aisha: Great.
[08:55] Sarah: Recap — I'll send runbook + comms + canary playbook by Friday (2026-03-06). Marcus sends benchmarks and sizing. BrightCare confirms retention + maintenance windows. We'll schedule the canary for week of 2026-03-18 pending confirmation.
[09:12] Liam: One more small ask — can you include step-by-step rollback commands for infra team? We need the exact commands copy/paste.
[09:20] Marcus: Yes. We'll include runbook commands and simple scripts.
[09:25] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:27] Sarah: Thanks, we'll follow up in email and attach artifacts.
[09:30] Aisha: Bye.
[09:31] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., 'KV catch' instead of 'KV cache', 'red wood' spacing), and speaker overlap during rapid questions.
